claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy.
The feedstock particle-size range is 15–45 μm.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces coatings of acceptable quality.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces inadequate coating thickness.
The proposed intervention is to use a nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm rather than the current shorter distance.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity at impact.
A longer spray distance provides additional acceleration time in the combustion jet.
Higher impact kinetic energy improves coating consolidation or splat formation.
Higher impact kinetic energy lowers particle rebound.
The increased spray distance will improve bonding or deposition efficiency.
The increased spray distance will reduce particle scattering.
The modified spray distance will produce a significantly thicker coating than the baseline.
The thicker coating will remain adherent.
The modified process will preserve acceptable coating quality.
The modified process will maintain minimal in-spray oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating will remain effective under thermal and oxidative conditions typical of high-temperature thermal-barrier service.

contradictions.description: The cited PMC10820071 record reports that increasing spray distance lowers particle kinetic energy at impact, whereas the hypothesis claims that increasing distance raises impact velocity and kinetic energy.

The cited PMC10820071 record reports stronger particle scattering and a slight decrease in coating thickness at longer spray distances, contrary to the proposed reduction in scattering and increase in thickness.
The cited PMC10820071 record reports increased porosity and oxide content with increasing spray distance, contrary to the prediction that coating quality and minimal oxidation will be preserved.
